title: Conduct Material Intake, Storage and Reclaim Operations

lessons.title: Running an intake shift
lessons.html:
Running an intake shift

This practical module is about doing intake, storage and reclaim work correctly and safely, step by step. Use your mill's SOPs; the steps below show the standard pattern.

Start of shift

  1. Attend the shift handover. Find out which silos are allocated to which material, levels in each, deliveries expected and any open faults.
  2. Check your PPE: safety boots, high-visibility vest, dust mask, hearing protection, gloves.
  3. Walk the intake area: pit grids in place, magnets clean, no spillage, lights working, fire extinguishers present.
  4. Check the intake route on the control screen or panel: elevator, conveyors and distributor set to the right silo.

Processing a delivery

  1. Direct the truck to the weighbridge. Record gross mass and check documents against the purchase order.
  2. Take probe samples from the load according to the sampling plan. Seal and label the sample with truck, supplier and time.
  3. Do the quick checks: smell, temperature, insects, foreign matter, moisture meter reading. Hand the sample to the laboratory if tests are required.
  4. Wait for release. Never off-load a load that has not been accepted.
  5. Direct the truck to the correct pit. Start the route (downstream equipment first) before the truck tips.
  6. Watch the off-loading: pit level, elevator load, any choke or alarm. Stop tipping if the pit overfills.
  7. Inspect the magnet and scalper after each load or as scheduled; record findings.
  8. Weigh the empty truck out. Complete the goods received record.

Safety at the pit

  • Keep clear of the truck when it reverses or lifts its tipper body. Use a banksman.
  • Never stand on or open pit grids while the pit is being fed.
  • Do not climb on a truck load; use the sampling platform with guardrails.

lessons.title: Storage checks and reclaiming to production
lessons.html:
Storage checks and reclaiming to production

Storage monitoring

  • Read silo levels and grain temperature at the set times and record them.
  • Report a rising temperature trend at once; it can mean moisture, insects or mould.
  • Run aeration fans when instructed, usually when outside air is cool and dry enough to cool the grain.
  • Check bagged stores: pallets intact, stack heights correct, FIFO order kept, no pest signs, quarantine area properly tagged.
  • Keep silo top and tunnel areas clean. Dust build-up is a fire and explosion hazard.

Reclaim

Reclaim means drawing material out of storage to the production bins.

  1. Confirm the production request: which ingredient, how much, to which production bin.
  2. Check the source silo holds the right material and grade, and the destination bin is allocated to that ingredient.
  3. Set and confirm the route; check distributor position on screen and, where possible, physically.
  4. Start the route downstream first, then open the silo outlet gate.
  5. Monitor flow, levels and alarms. Stop before the destination bin is overfull.
  6. Close the gate, run the route empty, then stop equipment upstream first.
  7. Record the transfer: source, destination, quantity, time.

Dealing with problems

ProblemAction
Elevator chokeStop feed, isolate and lock out, clear from the boot as the SOP says
Material bridging in siloUse external vibrators or approved methods; never enter the silo without a permit
Wrong material in a binStop, report, quarantine; do not let it go to production
Hot bearing or burning smellStop the equipment and report immediately

End of shift

Clean spillage, complete records and hand over: silo levels, deliveries received and outstanding, faults and unfinished transfers.

Key points

  • Never off-load a delivery before it has been accepted.
  • Confirm routes and bin allocation before every transfer.
  • Start downstream first, stop upstream first.
  • Monitor silo temperature and act on rising trends.
  • Never enter a silo to clear bridging without a permit.
